Ajmalul Hossain with Aminul Islam Monda, Advocates ----- For the Opposite Party No.1 Applicant. 
Maqbul Ahmed, Advocate ----- For the Petitioners.
parties:
MA Kabir Chowdhury and others ----- Petitioners
Vs.
M Mahbubur Rahman Miah & ors ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Md Abdur Rashid J: This application at the instance of the decree holder is made under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for recalling and/or vacating the direction given vide order dated 22-10-2001 by this Division in above Civil Order No. 5742 for stay of further proceedings in Other Execution Case No.3 of 1997 while disposing of a revision application of the above petitioners. 

 2. In the application: it is stated that decree-holder Md Mahbubur Rahman Mia instituted Title Suit No. 101 of 1989 for declaration of title and recovery of possession. The suit was then re- numbered as Other Suit No. 22 of 1992. On 29-10-95 the suit was decreed on contest. First Appeal No. 37 of 1996 preferred by the defendants from the decree was also dismissed by this Division by judgment and decree dated 29-10-2000. In the meantime, said decree holder already levied the decree in Other Execution Case No. 3 of 1997 before the Subordinate Judge and Second Commercial Court at Chittagong for possession. 

 4. On 25-7-2001 said Kabir Chowdhury and two others made an application under Order XXXIX rules 1 and 2 of the Code in their partition suit for temporary injunction for restraining said decree holder from executing the decree for possession. On 9-9-2001 the application was heard and rejected on contest. Similarly, their application for stay of further proceeding of the execution case was rejected on contest by the executing Court by its order dated 29-8-2001. 

 5. Then, on 18-9-2001 said Kabir Chowdhury and two others made a fresh application in their partition suit before Third Court of Subordinate Judge for temporary injunction for restraining the decree holder from executing the decree, which is still pending for hearing. On 20-9-2001 Kabir Chowdhury again made an application before the executing Court, Second Commercial Court of Subordinate Judge for stay of further proceeding of Other Execution Case 3 of 1997 till disposal of the Partition Suit and also for rejection of the execution proceeding. The application was heard and rejected on contest by the executing Court by its order dated 8-10-2001. 

 7. It is further stated that pursuant to the order of this Division, the learned Subordinate Judge, Second Commercial Court was obliged to stay further proceeding of Other Execution Case No. 3 of 1997. All steps of the decree holder for getting the application for temporary injunction heard over the period of last four months proved futile. 

 8. In the circumstances, the decree holder has come up with this application under section 151 of the Code before this Division for an order either recalling and/or vacating the direction dated 27-10-2001 as given in above Civil Order. 

 9. In the support of the application, Mr Ajmalul Hossain, learned Senior Counsel submits that in the revision application neither orders dated 29-8-2001 and 9-9-2001 rejecting the repeated prayers for stay or injunction were neither mentioned nor full and fair disclosure of the facts and circumstances leading the revision application made. By misleading as to the record and also by practicing fraud through suppression of those material facts said Kabir Chowdhury and two others as petitioners obtained the direction from this Division for stay of the execution proceeding. Thus, misled, the Division Bench, he further submits, fell in serious error of procedure in granting as order of stay of the execution proceeding while disposing of the revision application till disposal of an application for temporary injunction pending in a separate proceeding before another Court in the absence of the decree holder. This Division is therefore entitled to invoke inherent power to undo the wrong, which has seriously prejudiced the decree holder for no fault of his. In support, be cited the decisions in the case of Abdul Aziz vs Aboni Mohan, 30 DLR (SC) 21; Abdus Sattar Khodaker vs Prem Lata, 49 DLR 583 and Brink's Mat Ltd vs Elcombe and others, (1988) 1 WLR 1350. 

 10. Mr Moqbul Ahmed, learned Counsel for said Kabir Chowdhury and two others who as petitioners obtained the direction, opposed the application submitting that if the decree holder Mahbubur Rahman felt aggrieved by the order dated 22-10-2001 he could have preferred an appeal or prayed for review of the order in accordance with law. Without taking any such step, the application made under section 151 of the Code is not maintainable. After final disposal of the revision application, this Division has also got no jurisdiction to open the matter again by invoking inherent jurisdiction. On merit, he submits that the direction as given by this Division for stay of the execution does not suffer from any illegality in the facts and circumstances of the case as made out in the revision application. 

 12. In Abdus Sattar Khondaker vs Premlata, a single Bench of this Division confirmed an order of the trial Court which set aside an ex parte decree obtained against dead persons by suppressing summons upon the view. 

 "there are authorities which lay down that even after the passing of the decree, the court can entertain an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure in an appropriate case where fraud was practiced upon the court and in such case the question of becoming functus officio after the pronouncement of judgment and signing a decree does not arise at all because fraud vitiates everything." 

 "Fraud avoids all judicial acts, ecclesiastical or temporal"-observed Chief Justice Edward Coke of England about three centuries ago. It is the settled proposition of law that a judgment or decree obtained by playing fraud on the court is a nullity and non est in the eyes of law. Such a judgment/decree-by the first Court or by the highest court-has to be treated as a nullity by every Court, whether superior or inferior. It can be challenged in any Court even in collateral proceedings." 

 20. Now, turning to the facts of the case at hand, we find that the applicant on 29-10-95 obtained a decree in Other Suit No. 22 of 1992, declaring his title in the suit land and for recovery of possession of said land and First Appeal No.37 of 1996 preferred by the defendants before this Division was also dismissed on 29-10-2000. The decree was levied by the applicant-decree holder long back in Other Execution Case No. 3 of 1997 for recovery of possession of the suit land. On 12-9- 99 said Kabir Chowdhury and two others instituted Partition Suit No. 153 of 1999. They have claimed to take possession of the suit land from defendant No. 6 of the earlier suit who failed to resist the decree up to this Division. Their application under Order XXXIX rules 1 and 2 of the Code for temporary injunction made in their partition suit against the decree holder for restraining him from executing the decree was on 9-9-2001 rejected on contest by the Third Court of Subordinate Judge. The order is appealable, but they preferred no appeal therefrom. Instead, on 18-9-2001 they made a fresh application in their partition suit for temporary injunction for restraining the decree holder from executing the above decree till disposal of the suit, which is still pending for hearing. Their prayer for stay of further proceedings of Other Execution Case No.3 of 1997 before the Second Commercial Court of Subordinate Judge was also on 29-8-2001 rejected on contest. Without taking any step against such order, on 20-9-2001 they made a fresh application on the same ground before the executing Court for stay of further proceedings of the execution case till disposal of the partition suit, which was again rejected on contest of 8-10-2001. Against this second order rejecting the prayer for stay of the execution proceeding, said Kabir Chowdhury and two others on 22-10-2001 moved this Division in revision under section 115 of the Code. In the revision application, they did neither mention the order of Second Commercial Court of Subordinate Judge dated 29-8-2001 rejecting the application for stay nor the order of Third Subordinate Judge dated 9-9-2001 rejecting their application for temporary injunction made in the partition suit. Thus misleading as to the record by not-disclosure of the above material facts, they obtained an order of stay of further proceedings of Other Execution Case No. 3 of 1997 till disposal of their second application for temporary injunction and thereby, they obtained practically the full relief of stay behind the back of the decree holder. It is needless to say that fate of second application for temporary injunction for restraining the decree holder from executing the decree dated 29-10-95 tilt disposal 0 the partition suit against 119 persons is fore known. We do not have any hesitation to say that this Division would not have granted such stay had it known that the prayers of the petitioners of the revision application for stay of execution as well as temporary injunction were rejected on contest by both the Courts below. 

 21. The order dated 22-10-2001 also suffers from some infirmities. The proceeding for execution of the decree dated 29-1-95 is pending in Other Execution Case No. 3 of 1997 before the Subordinate Judge and Second Commercial Court while Partition Suit No. 153 of 1999 is pending before the Third Court of Subordinate Judge. Granting an order of stay of the execution proceeding till disposal of an application for temporary injunction made in the partition suit pending before another Court cannot be said to have been made in accordance with recognized procedure, particularly when the record of the partition suit was not before the Court. Such order of say of a long pending execution proceeding without issue of any rule is also not in conformity with the long-stating procedure of this Division. Little circumspection would have saved the decree holder from the situation he is now facing-the execution is stayed but nobody can say definitely when the temporary injunction matter would finally be disposed of. 

 22. In such situation, we cannot accept that this Division cannot exercise the power under section 151 of the Code. The submission that the remedy of the decree holder lies only in the statutory appeal or review has no substance, because in statutory appeal of review the issues are limited to the pleadings of the parties. When an order is passed by a Court on being misled as to record or under misapprehension of facts or due to its own mistake such issues cannot be raised or decided in appeal or review. A Court of law is obliged to correct the mistake when true facts are brought before it and make such order as necessary for ends of justice in exercise of the inherent jurisdiction. The Court must not allow its process to be abused by any such unscrupulous person.
